brief:
Human Rights Watch called on Sudanese authorities to immediately hand over former Interior Minister Ahmed Haroun to the International Criminal Court, saying he should face charges in The Hague for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity. Haroun was recently taken into custody in Sudan and is wanted by the ICC for conduct in Darfur dating to 2003 and 2004.

The organization's demand comes as Sudan holds a suspect wanted for some of the gravest alleged offenses under international law. Haroun's transfer would bring him before the court to answer for atrocities committed during the conflict in Darfur two decades ago.
dek: Sudanese authorities should immediately transfer former Interior Minister Ahmed Haroun to the International Criminal Court (ICC) to face charges in The Hague, Human Rights Watch said today. Haroun was recently taken into Sudanese custody and faces ICC war crimes and crimes against humanity charges, committed in Sudan’s Darfur region, in 2003 and 2004.
title: Human Rights Watch demands Sudan transfer war crimes suspect to ICC
